To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
corticosterone regulates 12 mRNAs in astrocytes.
corticosterone rapidly regulates the expression of at least ten mRNA species in primary type 2 rat astrocytes.

1) corticosterone rapidly regulates the expression of multiple proteins in primary type I astrocytes, 2) these changes are not due to alterations in protein stability, 3) two of the regulated proteins have been identified, and 4) the remaining proteins have been identified and will be the focus of future research.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of mRNAs and their corresponding proteins that are regulated by glucocorticoids in primary rat astroglial cultures.
the effects of glucocorticoid hormone on astrocytes, the most abundant cell type in the brain.
understanding the mechanisms of glucocorticoid hormone action in the central nervous system (CNS).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the glucocorticoids, corticosterone in the rat and cortisol in humans, are important in neuronal survival and function.
the glucocorticoid corticosterone is a potent regulator of gene expression in primary rat type 1 astrocytes.
corticosterone regulates a variety of proteins in rat astrocytes and that some of these are likely involved in astrocyte function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glucocorticoids are able to rapidly alter gene expression in primary rat astroglia, and the effects are both astrocyte- and cell-type specific.
corticosterone rapidly and specifically alters the expression of several mRNAs in astrocytes.
glucocorticoid receptors (GRs) in astrocytes are functional, and that they regulate the synthesis of proteins that are likely to be important for astrocyte physiology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
corticosterone, a glucocorticoid hormone, can alter gene expression in primary astrocytes.
corticosterone, a hormone that has been studied extensively in the context of its role in the stress response, also regulates the expression of many proteins in astrocytes.
astrocytes respond to corticosterone in the same way as neurons, with the same types of proteins being upregulated, but the magnitude of the change is much greater in astrocytes than in neurons.
